correctness.rationale: The arcsine law becomes uniform under x=sin²(πt/2); F(x)−x=x(3−4x) gives the sign cut at t=2/3, up to null endpoints and preimages. Each monotone tent branch used for an allowed sign transition covers the full target interval at constant absolute slope two. Consequently the conditional density given an entire permitted history is uniform on the last sign interval, proving the stationary Markov claim, not just two-symbol statistics. The weighted transition product counts the initial sign and each later sign exactly once. The centered sign is an eigenfunction at −1/2 with variance 8/9. The covariance sum T+2Σ_{k=1}^{T−1}(T−k)(−1/2)^k reduces to T/3+4(1−(−1/2)^T)/9, giving the boxed variance. The stationary row entropies and Fibonacci support give the claimed rates. These conclusions require the invariant law, not a fixed initial point. The frozen rational-cylinder checker was inspected, not rerun; its finite tests do not replace the conditional-law argument.
